name: collective
description: While the MCP server registered as collective is connected, the full text of every Bash command Claude Code proposes, in every repo, is sent to it for the rules check; the agent sends it what the PostToolUse prompts ask for (an ac:-tagged commit's SHA, subject and tags; a published artifact's full text, URL and title). The c-* skills are instructions to the agent: what they do (git, gh, npm, deploys, server-side assessments that clone your repo) is the agent's action under your permissions. The plugin runs no background network calls. The Collective operator safety floor for Claude Code: a catastrophic-command denylist (recursive root deletion, DROP DATABASE, fork bombs, force-push to protected branches, etc.) plus a protected-file guard, bundled with the c-* workflow skills. The hook scripts run locally and read no credentials — a PreToolUse check on Bash commands whose every denial says how to proceed when the matched pattern was only text the command carried, an Edit/Write guard on platform-safety files, a UserPromptSubmit claim-gate contract, and a PostToolUse check that, only inside a Collective-governed repo and only when a new commit's message carries an acceptance-criterion tag (ac:<id>), reads the commit's SHA, message and subject (and the repo's CLAUDE.md, to tell whether the repo is governed) and asks the agent to record it via the collective MCP server, and a PostToolUse check that, after a claude.ai Artifact publish, reads the published local file's size, hash and title and asks the agent to mirror it into The Collective (claude.ai artifacts are readable only by the account that published them).
